prompt:
A trolley of mass 2.0 kg is pulled along a straight horizontal track. A horizontal force F varies with displacement s as shown:
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Graph showing force F / N on the vertical axis against displacement s / m on the horizontal axis. From s = 0 to s = 4.0 m, F is constant at 30 N. From s = 4.0 m to s = 7.0 m, F decreases linearly from 30 N to 0 N.]
(a) Calculate the work done on the trolley during the first 4.0 m of displacement. [1]
(b) Calculate the work done on the trolley as it moves from s = 4.0 m to s = 7.0 m. [1]
(c) Determine the total work done on the trolley over the entire 7.0 m displacement. [1]
hints: In (a), find the area of the rectangular portion.
In (b), find the area of the triangular portion: 0.5 * base * height.
In (c), add the two areas together.
solution:
(a) Between s = 0 and s = 4.0 m, the force is constant at 30 N. Area_1 = base * height = 4.0 m * 30 N = 120 J.
(b) Between s = 4.0 m and s = 7.0 m, the force decreases linearly from 30 N to 0. Base = 7.0 - 4.0 = 3.0 m. Area_2 = 0.5 * base * height = 0.5 * 3.0 m * 30 N = 45 J.
(c) Total work done = Area_1 + Area_2 = 120 J + 45 J = 165 J.
teacher_walkthrough: Step (a) tests constant force rectangular area.
Step (b) tests linear variable force triangular area.
Step (c) reinforces compound area integration on force-displacement graphs.
